evidence_refs.label: Layered dielectric series closed form
evidence_refs.notes: Independent one-dimensional displacement-continuity solution for the three-region electrostatic fixture.

evidence_refs.label: Electrostatic structured mesh convergence
evidence_refs.notes: Real Rust solver runs at one, two, four, and eight quad elements per material layer.

evidence_refs.label: Harmonic dielectric-loss projection
evidence_refs.notes: Converts solved RMS dielectric fields into frequency-local volumetric loss and conservatively lumps the power to heat nodes.

evidence_refs.label: Temperature-dependent electrothermal feedback convergence
evidence_refs.notes: Retains every relaxed electrostatic-loss-heat iteration and gates regional temperature residual, successive loss change, and thermal-conductivity stability.

evidence_refs.label: Solved temperature-dependent conductor Joule heating
evidence_refs.notes: Solves conductor potential and current density, integrates subcell sigma-E-squared loss, recovers terminal reactions, and converts the conserved power into regional heat load.

evidence_refs.label: Layered thermal-resistance closed form
evidence_refs.notes: Independent downstream thermal-resistance solution for uniform dielectric generation and fixed right-edge temperature.

evidence_refs.label: Heat structured mesh convergence
evidence_refs.notes: Real Rust solver runs at one, two, four, and eight heat quads per material layer.

evidence_refs.label: Heat-field to thermal-strain projection
evidence_refs.notes: Maps solved nodal temperatures into structural temperature deltas after node identity and coordinate checks.

evidence_refs.label: Temperature-dependent thermal-expansion projection
evidence_refs.notes: Updates every declared structural region from its solved local mean temperature and gates complete region coverage.

evidence_refs.label: Thermal-structural two-dimensional mesh convergence
evidence_refs.notes: Real Rust solver runs at one, two, four, and eight subdivisions in both panel directions; displacement and strain energy control the gate.

evidence_refs.label: Thermal-structural observed order and GCI
evidence_refs.notes: Four refinement levels classify asymptotic behavior before permitting Richardson extrapolation or fine-grid GCI.

evidence_refs.label: Thermal-structural algebraic residual
evidence_refs.notes: Recomputes original-system residuals for every uniform, regularized, and graded mesh solve.

evidence_refs.label: Thermal-structural restraint sensitivity
evidence_refs.notes: Compares the full edge clamp with a roller edge and one vertical anchor without overriding the primary quality gates.

evidence_refs.label: Area-weighted thermal-stress recovery
evidence_refs.notes: Tracks area-weighted von Mises RMS and P95 convergence while retaining the raw maximum as a singularity diagnostic.

evidence_refs.label: Prototype material cards
evidence_refs.notes: Scalar room-temperature values for conductor, dielectric, and substrate families.

evidence_refs.label: Synthetic mixed-material panel fixture
evidence_refs.notes: Three-region quad panel used to validate mixed-material partitioned feedback coupling.

limitations: Electrothermal coupling uses a relaxed partitioned fixed point; a monolithic coupled Jacobian and mechanical-field feedback are not modeled yet.

Material regions use scalar isotropic linear temperature sensitivities for dielectric, conductivity, and expansion parameters; anisotropy, validated nonlinear curves, and delamination propagation are not modeled yet.

Electrical heating projects harmonic dielectric loss and solved conductor Joule loss; built-in temperature coefficients are screening sensitivities until material cards supply validated curves. Contact and terminal impedance operators are available but require explicit fixture mappings, while broadband dispersion remains outside this model.
Interface risk is a screening heuristic over CTE mismatch and stiffness contrast, not an adhesive fracture mechanics model.
The regularized restraint solve is diagnostic only; persistent strain-energy nonconvergence remains a qualification blocker.
Use this prototype for architecture validation and candidate ordering only, not qualification claims.

model_assumptions.impact: Iterates dielectric parameters and heat to a fixed point, but is not a monolithic multiphysics Jacobian.
model_assumptions.label: Partitioned electrothermal coupling
model_assumptions.value: electrostatic RMS field plus solved steady-current conductor loss <-> regional temperature feedback -> heat -> thermal stress

model_assumptions.impact: Built-in coefficients exercise feedback robustness and must be replaced by validated material-card curves for qualification.
model_assumptions.label: Screening temperature sensitivity
model_assumptions.value: linear epsilon_r(T), tan_delta(T), regional k(T), and regional alpha(T) coefficients

model_assumptions.impact: Represents dielectric heating at one screening frequency, not broadband dispersion.
model_assumptions.label: Frequency-local dielectric loss

model_assumptions.impact: The operator supports lumped contact resistance and impedance terminals with source-power balance, while this retained fixture activates only the bulk conductor path.
model_assumptions.label: Voltage-driven steady-current field

model_assumptions.impact: Fast to evaluate, but does not represent anisotropy or interfaces.
